atomicity.reason: One obligation - hold the contactor-open command and release it only on one named event; the second sentence restates the same obligation's consequence.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: it names the triggering fault class, the held output and the single release event.

feasibility.reason: A two-state latch with a diagnostic-service exit, exactly as the supervising architecture element describes; contradicts nothing else stated.

parent_fit.reason: Directly implements the parent story's statement that the pack stays disconnected until a qualified technician clears the fault and that an intermittent condition cannot silently re-close the circuit.

unambiguity.reason: It is not stated whether a diagnostic service reset releases the hold while the violating measurement is still outside its limit, so a competent reader can take the reset as unconditional or as gated on the condition having cleared - a safety-relevant difference.
unambiguity.suggestion: State explicitly whether a reset received while a limit is still violated is rejected (or immediately re-latches), and what the contactor state is on release.

verifiability.reason: Testable end to end: trigger a fault, return measurements into range and confirm the hold persists, then send the reset and confirm release.

summary: Correctly captures the parent's 'stays disconnected until a technician clears it' promise; the one gap is whether a reset is honoured while a limit is still violated.
